answer.short: Acute: isosceles C; equilateral I, B; scalene E, G. Right: isosceles F; equilateral none; scalene A. Obtuse: isosceles D; equilateral none; scalene H.
answer.worked:
A: right-angled and scalene—one angle is $90^{\circ}$ and the angles are unequal.

B: acute and equilateral—all three angles are $60^{\circ}$.

C: acute and isosceles—two angles are $70^{\circ}$.

D: obtuse and isosceles—one angle is $130^{\circ}$ and two angles are $25^{\circ}$.

E: acute and scalene—the angles $72^{\circ}$, $74^{\circ}$ and $34^{\circ}$ are all acute and unequal.

F: right-angled and isosceles—one angle is $90^{\circ}$ and two angles are $45^{\circ}$.

G: acute and scalene—the angles $61^{\circ}$, $59^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ are all acute and unequal.

H: obtuse and scalene—one angle is $92^{\circ}$ and all three angles are unequal.

I: by symmetry, the reflected base angles are both $60^{\circ}$ and the vertex half-angles are both $30^{\circ}$. Hence all three angles are $60^{\circ}$, so triangle I is acute and equilateral.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why the ‘equilateral column’ has two blank boxes.

answer.worked: Every equilateral triangle has three $60^{\circ}$ angles. Each angle is less than $90^{\circ}$, so an equilateral triangle cannot be right-angled or obtuse.

children.prompt: Identify the type of triangle based on the following information:

inlines.text: A triangle with all sides and angles equal

answer.worked: All three sides are equal, so the triangle is equilateral.

inlines.text: A triangle with no sides equal

answer.worked: All three side lengths are different, so the triangle is scalene.
All three angles are different, so the triangle is scalene. Since $103^{\circ}>90^{\circ}$, it is also obtuse.
Two sides have length $11$, so the triangle is isosceles.
